newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Top Clinton aide meets Russian ministers.
newsitem.headline: Top Clinton aide meets Russian ministers.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott held talks in Russia on Thursday with Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.

The discussions were aimed at preparing the ground for a meeting in Washington next month between Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and U.S. Vice-President Al Gore, a U.S. embassy spokesman told Reuters.
They also touched on a summit in the United States in March between President Bill Clinton and President Boris Yeltsin, he added.
Russian news agencies said Talbott's talks included NATO's planned eastward expansion, which Moscow fiercely opposes as a threat to its security.
"This problem can be resolved positively in the interests of both Russia and of NATO but we need to work on it," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Rodionov as saying after his talks with Talbott.
Tass quoted Talbott as saying that NATO enlargement was "a very important and difficult issue".
"We understand each other quite well and will work together to find a solution," Talbott added.

Talbott's talks came a day after Primakov firmly restated Moscow's views on NATO expansion. Primakov also said any future document that aimed to define relations between Russia and the Atlantic alliance should be legally binding.
The Russian Foreign Ministry said on Thursday Primakov was likely to meet the new U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright "in the near future".
